missionPremise: An ETJ is by definition outside city limits. P-332 measured that exactly three published rings in the six counties contain their own city's representative point (georgetown-tx:9644, leander-tx:7305, dripping-springs-tx:1), and that 24 of the 355 rings are invalid, so ST_Contains was being run against polygons nothing had verified. Confirmed at source in this lane: 355 rows, 355 distinct etj_ids, 24 invalid (the dry run's own identity query, agreeing with P-332 exactly), and the same three rings pass the decisive test ST_Contains(ring, ST_PointOnSurface(city_limits)).
completionPredicate: An ingest keeps the publisher's geometry verbatim and writes a SERVED geometry plus a derivation record; the reader runs containment only against a proven-testable served geometry and refuses (rather than tests) a ring that is underived, excluded or withheld, declaring why; a repair that moves the area past a declared tolerance is excluded, not served. Falsifiable in both directions on fixtures (done: 5 failed pre-change, 5 passed post-change) and measurable read-only against the store (done: the six-county re-count, the per-ring verdicts and the genuine-strip population). The part this lane cannot complete is the live customer read, because it cannot deploy or re-ingest.

As first written this said the figures were ring-level counts that a parcel inside two different cities' rings would inflate, and that the parcel-level answer was the shape that spills on this compute. threeQuestionGate.whatExecutes: the derivation: deriveEtjServedGeometry (lib/cad-ingest/src/boundary/etjDerive.ts), called by upsertEtjBoundaries for exactly the city keys just written; the validity refusal: buildEtjBoundaryIndex + resolveEtjAtPoint (lib/cad-ingest/src/boundary/containment.ts), reached from artifacts/api-server/src/lib/etjFactRead.ts on every determination. One implementation of the rule, two callers.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggers: an ingest run per publisher, and every ETJ determination a customer request makes. A ring PUBLISHED AFTER this change goes through the same path: inserted under the fail-closed default `underived`, derived in the same call, and only then servable. If the derivation statement throws, the ingest fails and any flushed rows stay `underived`, which the reader refuses and declares — asserted by the integration fixture 'unrun-city-tx:1' (a publisher this run did not name keeps `underived`).
threeQuestionGate.whatFails: a ring that reaches the reader as `underived`, `excluded` or `withheld`, or that claims a servable status while carrying no testable Polygon/MultiPolygon, becomes a refusal; any point such a ring could have covered resolves `unresolved` with the refusal's own reason, never `present` and never `absent`. LESSON: A self-check that iterates the INSTRUMENT'S OWN output cannot detect that the instrument was truncated. The H dedup's ring-by-ring cross-check against the E section printed `mismatches: 0` over a Travis run that had been killed mid-flight, and reported 0 / 0 / 0 where the answer is 87 / 44 / 43 — because it looped over the rings present in its own (partial) output and never over the rings that were missing. The pass was manufactured by the defect. Corroborate against a counter written independently of the instrument's output — the E section's per-ring columns, or an identity like pre = post + refused — and check row counts against an expected cardinality, or the clean self-check is worse than no self-check.

A hand-written total in a close is not a measurement and does not fail loudly: the two cross-county aggregate queries that could have produced this lane's own total both died (one on statement_timeout at 900s, one on 'Disk quota exceeded') while the six per-county runs all exited 0, so the total was written by hand and disagreed with the rows above it by one on each column. Sum the instrument's own rows in the instrument, or print the total from the query that produced the rows.

On a Neon read-only compute, statement_timeout IS the instrument's exclusion set. A per-ring scalar subquery over a MATERIALIZED CTE finishes (no index on a CTE, so it is a bounded seq scan per ring) while the parcel-level non-equi join with bool_or over the same CTE spills and dies. Split the aggregate, report the part that fits, and name the part that did not — a query that returns partial output and exit 0 is the worst case.

When a query is too heavy, EMIT THE ROWS IN THE SHAPE THAT ALREADY FINISHES instead of rewriting it into a cheaper-looking one. The cross-city parcel total was attempted three times as an aggregate: the original non-equi join with bool_or (900s timeout), a per-parcel EXISTS (cross_g, timeout), and a materialized `candidates` CTE that prefiltered parcels by the rings' envelopes (cross_i, killed at 8 minutes — in Travis the prefilter removed almost nothing, because Austin's rings reach most of the county). The one that worked was the original E section's own correlated subquery, unchanged, with `unnest(ARRAY(...))` in place of count(*) — 44.7s for Travis, all six counties in 122s. A rewritten plan is a different query with different costs; the plan you already measured is evidence, and 'cheaper' is a hypothesis until it runs.

A gate's coverage is per-checkout. probe-close-gate.mjs declares OPS24_RANGES [[186,198],[200,250],[252,320],[327,356],[358,365]] in P:/doc_repo and only [[186,198],[200,250],[252,320]] in C:/Users/cente/doc_repo, so the same close is gated in one worktree and silently SKIPPED (no verdict, no debt note) in the other.
